value.text:
Eleven tackles a game is a Hall of Fame habit, and Daren Teamer has never broken it.

Teamer has played 246 games in the secondary and made 2,740 tackles, a little more than 11 every time he takes the field. He has 42 interceptions to go with them. There is not a single sack or forced fumble on his line. He does not gamble on the big hit. He reads the play, arrives on time and finishes it, snap after snap.

The league named him Defensive Player of the Year once. He has never won a ring, and in Y89 his Bills went out in the wild card round in Cincinnati. The title has eluded him. The work has not.

He crossed into the Hall in Y89, still playing and still adding to the count. Daren Teamer, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Four Super Bowl rings on the Atlanta line.

Calais Ham arrived on the Falcons line in Y84. He has played 117 games and been credited with 262 blocks, more than two and a quarter a game. Few linemen have done more with every snap.

The rings came one after another under Dorren Skura, in Y84, Y85, Y86 and Y87, the last of them at the end of a perfect 17-0 season and a 30-21 win in Super Bowl CXLVI. Ham was in front for all of it, without an MVP or a Player of the Year award, because linemen do not win those.

He arrives in the Y87 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Calais Ham, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him.

Kalif Suh has played 263 games and made 841 tackles, with 17 interceptions, 24 sacks and 10 forced fumbles. That is a linebacker who does a little of everything: about three tackles a game, a takeaway when an offense gets careless, and pressure when the call comes to go get the quarterback.

He won three rings in New York, in Y77, Y80 and Y82, all on Dorren Skura's teams. When Skura left for Atlanta, Suh stayed, and he has kept the Jets defense steady ever since.

He arrives under the higher bar of Career Legacy 7,500, the second player inducted under it after Juwann Gilman. Kalif Suh, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Seven rings, and the best rushing seasons the record board has ever seen.

Ryland Maxwell came into the league with the Jets in Y80 and was Rookie of the Year, winning titles in Y80 and Y82. When Dorren Skura left for Atlanta after Y82, Maxwell went with him, and the Falcons won every season from Y83 through Y87.

In 192 games he has carried the ball 2,368 times for 17,716 yards and 253 touchdowns, and caught 117 passes for 892 yards and 32 more. He owns the single-game rushing record at 237 yards, the single-season touchdown record at 39 and the single-season yardage record at 2,670, set in Y87. Two Offensive Player of the Year awards and three Super Bowl MVPs say he saves his best for the biggest stage.

Ryland Maxwell, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
